newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW-CU SEES POLAND AS REGION'S CENTRE.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-CU SEES POLAND AS REGION'S CENTRE.

text.p: Britain's Commercial Union Plc (CU), which arrived in Poland in 1992, sees it as a foothold for expansion in the central and eastern Europe, CU's Polish unit president said on Thursday.

Marian Miziolek, in charge of CU operations in the region, told Reuters in an interview that the company would launch services in the Czech Republic in January 1997 and later planned entering Slovakia, Romania, Russia and Ukraine.

"The succes we experienced in Poland made us think of expanding our activity on the whole eastern and central Europe.... We want Poland to be a spring-board between Great Britain and the region," he said.
Poland will be a centre for employees training and transferring know-how to the region's countries, he said.

Polish Commercial Union Towarzystwo Ubezpieczen na Zycie Polska SA, in which the British CU holds 90 percent and Polish Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) holds 10 percent, controls 10.2 percent of Poland's life insurance market.
It ranks second among Polish life-insurers after Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU) Zycie, a subsidary of the non-life state-owned PZU giant. PZU Zycie has about 80 percent of the market.
Miziolek said CU would begin with life insurance operations in all countries of the region and later, after becoming familiar with the markets, it would offer non-life services.
He also said he saw vast possibilities for further expansion in life insurance in Poland thanks to Poles growing needs, higher incomes and the market's potential.
"There are 13 million working people in Poland and only one million individually insured ... the market is so unsaturated that life insurance companies have great opportunities to develop," he said.
"If we achieve 12 percent of the market in 1997, 13 percent in 1998 and 15 percent in 2000 we will be happy...," he added.
In the first three quarters of 1996 the company collected 212.2 million zlotys in gross premiums and had a net profit of 15.8 million zlotys.
In the whole 1995 it had 119.5 million zlotys in gross premiums and showed a net profit of 6.8 million.
